newsitem.title: THAILAND: Baht firms late, interbank rate drops further.
newsitem.headline: Baht firms late, interbank rate drops further.

text.p: The Thai baht firmed slightly in late trading on Friday as the greenback slipped against the yen while the overnight interbank rate dropped further on rising liquidity, dealers said.
The baht was bid/offered at 26.076-26.081 late against 26.082/26.085 in the morning in moderate trading. The central bank had earlier set a mid-rate of 26.08 baht to the dollar.
Dealers said the baht was not under selling pressure as the country's current account and trade deficits improved substantially in February due to a slowdown in the economy and in imports.

"It doesn't matter that they narrowed for the wrong reasons. They helped reduce pressure on the baht anyway. The movement of the baht now reflects the dollar/major trend more than the external balance," said one dealer at a U.S. bank.
The interbank rate edged down further to 7.25-6.75 percent late from 7.75-8.00 percent in the morning, dealers said.
The market was flushed with liquidity as banks attracted by low premiums, sold dollars through the swap market while demand for funds was low, they said.
The one month baht/dolalr swap premium was steady at 4.10/5.10 satang per dollar late against 4.00/5.00 satang in the morning.
"The rate could have been lower if the central bank did not absorb the liquidity through open market operations," said a dealer from Thai Farmers Bank.

The Bank of Thailand's Governor Rerngchai Marakanon said on Friday that the central bank does not want the interbank rate to fall below eight percent as it wants the money market to maintain high premiums to attract foreign inflows.
Dealers also took note of his statement that there were possibilities for Thai interest rates to ease as interbank rates were stabilising in the money market.
